patch_description: For a fixed set of centers, the optimal radii are obtained from a linear program: each radius has a wall upper bound, and every pair contributes the linear inequality r_i + r_j <= distance(i,j). The nonlinear SLSQP stage can stop with a suboptimal radius allocation even when its centers are promising, especially in asymmetric defect layouts. Re-solving this small LP after every center optimization extracts the best feasible varying-radius allocation from that contact geometry. The existing common-scale polish is retained afterward to certify strict feasibility against numerical tolerances.
